# A customer prepays 100 USD and the money arrives converted, as CAD.
#
# The book now owes 100 USD and holds no USD anywhere: the bank took CAD. The
# credit on the receivable is the only record of the currency, so it is the
# one that carries the cost basis — 1.37 CAD/USD, the rate the obligation was
# taken on. What a basis totals and what an account holds need not agree.
#
# `lot_owner:` is what makes this a prepayment rather than a settlement. The
# two are otherwise the same three lines (see fx_settlement_arriving_as_cad.txt),
# and a hand-written split that names no owner belongs to no lot, which is how
# a settlement looks.
#
# What this fixture produces: `fx-balances` lists the receivable credit,
# 100.00 USD at 1.37 CAD/USD, available in full.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable USD
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

customer "C-US"
	name: "US Customer"
	currency: USD

2026-02-01 * "Customer prepaid 100 USD, arriving as CAD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank 137.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "137.00"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.37"
		value: "-137.00"
		lot_owner: "customer:C-US"
